title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #15

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence helps you remember the cardinal points in clockwise order? (1 mark)
   A. Eat Slowly Now Wisely
   B. Never Eat Slimy Worms
   C. Some Old Men Walk
   D. Watch Every Sunny Night

2. Which direction is Nakuru from Nairobi? (1 mark)
   A. North-west
   B. East
   C. South-east
   D. South

3. On a map, the market is drawn above the school. Which direction is the market from the school? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. West
   C. South
   D. East

4. What do we call describing where a county is by naming the places around it? (1 mark)
   A. Relative location
   B. Rainfall
   C. Scale
   D. Population

5. What do we call the smaller parts into which a sub-county is divided? (1 mark)
   A. Wards
   B. Plateaus
   C. Oceans
   D. Continents

6. Which of these is built by people, not natural? (1 mark)
   A. A plain
   B. A dam
   C. A hill
   D. A river

7. During the dry season herders in dry areas often do what? (1 mark)
   A. Collect rainwater
   B. Move animals to find water and grass
   C. Sell umbrellas
   D. Plant maize

8. Which clothing helps drivers to see you on a rainy day? (1 mark)
   A. Black clothes
   B. Dark grey clothes
   C. Bright or reflective clothes
   D. Brown clothes

9. Why do farmers plan their work using seasons? (1 mark)
   A. Seasons decide the colour of soil
   B. Seasons tell the price of clothes
   C. Seasons decide school holidays only
   D. Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested

10. Which disease can spread more easily in wet weather because mosquitoes breed in puddles? (1 mark)
   A. Toothache
   B. Sunburn
   C. Malaria
   D. Broken leg

11. Which of these is not a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A cultural centre
   B. A museum
   C. A natural river
   D. A monument

12. What is a monument? (1 mark)
   A. A structure built to remember a person or event
   B. A river
   C. A market
   D. A bus

13. Which of these actions helps to conserve a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Reporting anyone who damages it
   B. Climbing on old walls
   C. Leaving litter
   D. Breaking off small pieces

14. Which is the best source of information about a historic place near you? (1 mark)
   A. An advert for soap
   B. A rumour
   C. A guess
   D. A resource person such as an elder or a guide

15. What is a museum? (1 mark)
   A. A bus stage
   B. A kind of factory
   C. A building where old objects are kept and shown
   D. A place where crops are grown

16. Which of these is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A pair of shoes
   B. Treatment by a nurse
   C. A bag of maize
   D. A book

17. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a farmer give? (1 mark)
   A. Health care
   B. Learning
   C. Transport
   D. Food

18. On a dot map, what does a group of many dots close together show? (1 mark)
   A. A road
   B. A river
   C. An empty area
   D. A crowded area

19. In a bar graph of sub-county populations, which sub-county has the tallest bar? (1 mark)
   A. The one with the fewest people
   B. The smallest area
   C. The largest area
   D. The one with the most people

20. Who usually passes traditional culture on to children? (1 mark)
   A. Only strangers
   B. Only shops
   C. Machines
   D. Parents, grandparents and elders

21. Which artefacts are carved at Kisii and sold to visitors? (1 mark)
   A. Soapstone carvings
   B. Plastic toys
   C. Glass windows
   D. Iron bridges

22. What is a kiondo? (1 mark)
   A. A basket
   B. A drum
   C. A house
   D. A shirt

23. Why do we recite the school motto? (1 mark)
   A. To hide
   B. To remember what the school stands for
   C. To scare others
   D. To waste time

24. What is a gallery walk? (1 mark)
   A. A cooking lesson
   B. A kind of assembly
   C. Walking round to look at displayed work
   D. A race

25. What is a good thing to do at the end of a project? (1 mark)
   A. Blame others
   B. Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   C. Throw away records
   D. Forget about it

26. What is discrimination? (1 mark)
   A. Treating everyone equally
   B. Helping
   C. Sharing
   D. Treating some people unfairly because of who they are

27. What is a right? (1 mark)
   A. Something every person is allowed to have or do
   B. A game
   C. A chore
   D. A punishment

28. At what age can a person legally marry in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 14 years
   B. 16 years
   C. 12 years
   D. 18 years

29. What does democracy mean? (1 mark)
   A. No rules
   B. Rule by the people
   C. Rule by one person
   D. Rule by force

30. What is a ballot paper? (1 mark)
   A. A menu
   B. A kind of book
   C. A ticket for a bus
   D. A paper on which a voter marks a choice

31. Which of these is a benefit of democracy in school? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils are ignored
   B. Leaders are never checked
   C. Only some pupils are heard
   D. Everyone has a voice

32. How often are general elections held in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Every month
   B. Every year
   C. Every five years
   D. Every ten years

33. How many tally marks does a group of five look like? (1 mark)
   A. One line
   B. Two lines
   C. Four lines crossed by one line
   D. Six lines

34. What does a patron do? (1 mark)
   A. Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   B. Drives the bus
   C. Cooks for pupils
   D. Wins all elections

35. Which item usually comes first on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Closing remarks
   B. Suggestions
   C. Opening prayer or song
   D. Reports

36. Why is it important for leaders to have good qualities? (1 mark)
   A. People trust them and live in peace
   B. People fear them
   C. People quarrel
   D. Resources are wasted

37. Who leads a sub-location? (1 mark)
   A. Governor
   B. Assistant chief
   C. President
   D. Speaker

38. How can you show respect for community leaders? (1 mark)
   A. Listen politely and follow fair rules
   B. Spread rumours
   C. Insult them
   D. Refuse to attend meetings

39. Which duty belongs to a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. Making laws
   B. Selling goods
   C. Leading prayers and teaching values
   D. Repairing cars

40. Which law created county governments in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A market rule
   B. The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   C. A church rule
   D. A school rule

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State three functions of the Children's Government. (3 marks)

42. Explain why many factories are built near big towns. (3 marks)

43. Name the four in-between points on a compass and say between which cardinal points each lies. (4 marks)

44. Draw a compass rose and label the four cardinal points. (3 marks)

45. Give two reasons why some areas are sparsely populated. (2 marks)

46. Explain how a cultural centre is different from a museum. (3 marks)

47. Give three rules for using safe school transport. (3 marks)

48. Give two reasons why some areas are densely populated. (2 marks)

49. Explain what may happen in a community with dishonest leaders. (3 marks)

50. Give three ways in which the rainy season helps people. (3 marks)

51. Name two historic places in Kenya and the town or county where each is found. (2 marks)

52. Draw a side view of the land showing a mountain, a valley and a plain and label them. (5 marks)

53. Name the four cardinal points. (2 marks)

54. Explain what a raw material is and give one example. (2 marks)

55. A group spent Ksh 350 on seeds and Ksh 150 on tools. They sold vegetables for Ksh 800. Find the profit. Show working. (3 marks)

56. Describe how you would design a safety bib for pupils who walk to school. (4 marks)

57. List four questions you could ask to find out the history of your school. (4 marks)

58. Explain why early marriage is against the rights of a child. (5 marks)

59. Explain why a monument is built. (2 marks)

60. What does the Kiswahili word amani mean and why is it important in a school? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Never Eat Slimy Worms
   The first letters N, E, S, W give north, east, south, west in clockwise order.

2. A — North-west
   Nakuru is north-west of Nairobi.

3. A — North
   Above means north when north is at the top.

4. A — Relative location
   Relative location compares a place with its neighbours.

5. A — Wards
   Sub-counties are divided into wards.

6. B — A dam
   A dam is built by people to hold water.

7. B — Move animals to find water and grass
   Grass and water become scarce, so herders move.

8. C — Bright or reflective clothes
   Bright and reflective clothes stand out.

9. D — Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested
   Planting and harvesting depend on rain and dry weather.

10. C — Malaria
   Mosquitoes that spread malaria breed in standing water.

11. C — A natural river
   A river is a natural feature, not built by people.

12. A — A structure built to remember a person or event
   Monuments remind people of important people or events.

13. A — Reporting anyone who damages it
   Reporting damage helps protect the place.

14. D — A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   Elders and guides know the true story of the place.

15. C — A building where old objects are kept and shown
   Museums keep artefacts safely and show them to people.

16. B — Treatment by a nurse
   A service is work done for someone. The others are goods.

17. D — Food
   Farmers give food to the community.

18. D — A crowded area
   Many dots show many people.

19. D — The one with the most people
   Taller bars show bigger values.

20. D — Parents, grandparents and elders
   Culture is taught in families and communities.

21. A — Soapstone carvings
   Kisii is known for soapstone carving.

22. A — A basket
   The kiondo is a woven basket.

23. B — To remember what the school stands for
   Reciting reminds us of the school's aims.

24. C — Walking round to look at displayed work
   In a gallery walk pupils look at each other's displays.

25. B — Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   Evaluation helps us do better next time.

26. D — Treating some people unfairly because of who they are
   Discrimination is unfair treatment.

27. A — Something every person is allowed to have or do
   Rights protect people.

28. D — 18 years
   The law says a person must be 18 to marry.

29. B — Rule by the people
   Democracy means the people have a say.

30. D — A paper on which a voter marks a choice
   Voters mark ballot papers.

31. D — Everyone has a voice
   Democracy makes everyone heard.

32. C — Every five years
   Kenya holds general elections every five years.

33. C — Four lines crossed by one line
   A group of five has four vertical lines and one crossing them.

34. A — Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   The patron is a teacher adviser.

35. C — Opening prayer or song
   Meetings begin with an opening.

36. A — People trust them and live in peace
   Good leaders build trust and peace.

37. B — Assistant chief
   An assistant chief leads a sub-location.

38. A — Listen politely and follow fair rules
   Respect means polite listening and obeying good rules.

39. C — Leading prayers and teaching values
   Religious leaders lead worship.

40. B — The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   The 2010 Constitution created counties.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent pupils, help keep order, and promote cleanliness. Accept organising activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each function.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Many customers live there. Workers live nearby. Roads and other services are available.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: North-east (between north and east), south-east (between south and east), south-west (between south and west), north-west (between north and west).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct in-between point with its place.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat drawing, 1 mark for N at top, 1 mark for E, S and W correct.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Very little rain and no water, and thick forests, swamps or steep land. Accept game parks or few roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A museum mainly keeps and shows objects. A cultural centre lets people see and join in living culture such as dances and crafts. Some places do both.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use only transport approved by the school and parents, do not take lifts from strangers, and do not board overloaded vehicles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Good rain and fertile soil for farming, and jobs and services in towns. Accept water or good roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Resources are wasted, people lose trust, and people quarrel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Crops grow, grass grows for animals, and rivers and tanks fill with water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fort Jesus in Mombasa and Thimlich Ohinga in Migori County. Accept Lamu Old Town or Gede Ruins.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct place with its location.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with a high peak labelled mountain, a low dip labelled valley and a flat area labelled plain.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape drawn and 1 mark for each label, up to 5 marks.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: North, east, south and west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct points, 2 marks for all four.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: A raw material is a material used to make something new, for example sugarcane used to make sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 300.
   Working / marking points: Cost = 350 + 150 = 500. Profit = 800 - 500 = 300. 1 mark for cost, 1 mark for subtraction, 1 mark for answer.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use bright cloth, cut it in a vest shape with a head opening, fix reflective strips across the front and back, and test that it is easy to wear and seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: When was the school started? Who started it? Who was the first headteacher? How has the school changed?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each relevant question.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: It stops a child from going to school. It harms health. It takes away childhood and play. It is against the law because the age of marriage is 18. It limits the child's future.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A monument is built to remind people of an important person or event so that they remember it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reminding people, 1 mark for the idea of a person or event.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Amani means peace. It is important because pupils feel safe and can learn well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 mark for the reason.
